key_insight: Combining 3D welding simulation with neural networks identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process-window selection to reduce weld defects, thermal gradients and axial force fluctuations in HDPE joints.
method: Model heat, forces, material flow and void formation using a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian simulation.
Train two multilayer perceptron networks on experimental temperature and axial force histories.
Use simulation and ANN predictions to map defective and defect-free welding conditions.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation showed good simulation agreement, ANN R² values of 0.91–0.99, and a peak plunge-force reduction from 1600 N to about 1100 N with 60 °C bottom preheating.
watch_item: Performance beyond the tested welding parameter space remains unverified and requires additional validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
